correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier block determinant is computed by direct substitution; the Chebyshev product yields the stated signed determinant for every integer q>=2. All zero blocks are rank one and occur as an exact conjugate pair, giving nullity two. The norm maximum and simple-zero minimum are derived from nonnegative 2x2 block singular values and their product. Relative Taylor error is uniform for the nearest frequency, even at Liouville approximations. Continued-fraction arguments give rational, badly approximable, Liouville alternatives. The delivered script confirmed 242 direct dense-matrix, symbolic rational, numerical singular-value and asymptotic assertions; these are supportive finite tests, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: A mass-preserving positive local blur is a natural inverse problem. The result provides a complete explicit finite-grid identifiability census and leading-order worst-case noise amplification in a simple spatially varying model, distinguishing rational, badly approximable and Liouville Fourier resonances. Those distinctions are relevant to how resolution changes affect deconvolution regularization. It does not assert actual floating-point failure, mean-case noise degradation or applicability to arbitrary point-spread functions.
